thread:
Allison Grant: For the unit economics dashboard work — we need explicit data quality SLOs before we wire paging. Right now we have “daily partitions” + “reconciliation job” but no agreed freshness/completeness targets. 

What are we targeting for:
1) freshness (t-1 partition ready by when?)
2) completeness (late events/backfill window)
3) reconciliation tolerance vs billing/metering

Also: who owns the oncall for these alerts? I don’t want #eng-sre getting paged for a pipeline schema change w/ no runbook. @Logan Wright @Nadia Rahman @Caleb Johnson @Aisha Bello

Aisha Bello: +1. For monitors we can split into “notify in Slack” vs “page”. But we need numbers. Proposed strawman (happy to adjust):
- Freshness SLO: `unit_econ_daily` partition for D is available by D+1 10:00 UTC (i.e., 26h max lag) 99% of days.
- Completeness SLO: >= 99.5% of metering events for D ingested/attributed by D+1 10:00 UTC. Late-arrival backfill runs for D-1..D-3 (72h window).
- Reconciliation SLO: abs( dashboard_total_cost - billing_total_cost ) / billing_total_cost <= 1.0% per day, and <= 0.5% on rolling 7-day.

Alerting:
- Freshness warn: 30 min past SLO in Slack (#eng-platform + #eng-sre)
- Freshness page: 2h past SLO to Telemetry/Analytics oncall
- Reconciliation warn: > 0.75% for 2 consecutive days
- Reconciliation page: > 1.5% any single day OR > 1.0% for 3 consecutive days

Ownership: I think “Telemetry/Analytics Platform” owns pages; SRE gets Slack visibility + helps tune.

Logan Wright: This looks reasonable. One nuance: we have two layers:
- raw metering ingestion (near-real-time)
- attribution + allocation (batch, daily)

Most misses will be attribution job running late. I’d rather define SLO on *published semantic view* since that’s what the dashboard reads.

For the time: D+1 10:00 UTC is okay, but Finance asked for this in the weekly review Monday morning PT. We should ensure weekends don’t drift.

Also: completeness at 99.5% might be aggressive on days with provider delays (esp eu-west metering). But I’m fine if backfill window covers it and we’re clear that t-1 is “provisional” for 72h.

Nadia Rahman: Agree on “semantic view SLO”. On completeness: we currently see ~0.3–0.8% late events within first 24h in eu-west when traffic spikes. It’s not loss, it’s late.

Maybe we define two metrics:
- `completeness_t1`: % events present by D+1 10:00 UTC (target 99.0%)
- `completeness_72h`: % events present by D+3 10:00 UTC (target 99.9%)

And we only page on `completeness_72h` misses (actual loss) vs t-1 being “yellow”.

Allison Grant: That split makes a lot of sense (t-1 provisional vs final). Paging on t-1 completeness misses is going to be noisy.

Can we also explicitly track “partitions missing” vs “partition present but incomplete”? Different failure modes.

Caleb Johnson: Yup. In Datadog we can set monitors on:
- partition existence (no row for `ds=D` by deadline)
- rowcount delta (today vs 7d median) by region/tier for gross anomalies
- late events rate (counts arriving for D-1..D-3)
- reconciliation variance

Re: partition present but incomplete: we can compute a “coverage ratio” = attributed_events / metering_events at D+1 and D+3. That’s basically Nadia’s completeness.

Thomas Baird: On thresholds: can we avoid alerting per model/region/tier? Cardinality will kill us. Recommend monitors only on global + by region (top-level), and dashboard drilldowns for the rest.

If we page, it should be on global/regional aggregates, not per-model. 

Aisha Bello: +1 to low-cardinality monitors.

Also for paging thresholds: 2h past deadline seems fine, but if this blocks Monday morning review we may want a tighter “business hours” policy (page earlier on Mon 07:00 PT). We can add a schedule-aware check later.

Priya Natarajan: On ownership: Telemetry/Analytics (Logan/Nadia team) owns pipeline + pages. SRE (Allison/Aisha) owns monitor implementation patterns + alert hygiene.

Let’s do:
- Pages -> PagerDuty service `telemetry-analytics` (or create `unit-econ-data` if we want a dedicated rotation)
- Slack alerts -> #eng-platform and #eng-sre
- Finance visibility -> optional #finance ping only on reconciliation > 1.5% (non-paging) so they’re not surprised

Runbook link required before paging goes live.

Logan Wright: We can create a lightweight runbook section in the existing unit-econ runbook (backfill + common failures). We’ll add:
- “partition missing: check Airflow DAG `unit_econ_daily_agg`”
- “reconciliation spike: check region mapping + late partitions; try excluding D-0/D-1”
- “schema drift: recent deploys in metering ingestion”

Action: Nadia + Mei can write first pass; Caleb can add monitor screenshots.

Nadia Rahman: Proposed final SLO wording (edits welcome):
- Freshness (provisional): For each day D, the semantic view `unit_econ.daily_blended_cost` contains partition D by D+1 10:00 UTC in 99% of days.
- Completeness (provisional): coverage_ratio(D, D+1) >= 99.0% overall and >= 98.5% for any single region.
- Completeness (final): coverage_ratio(D, D+3) >= 99.9% overall and >= 99.7% per region.
- Reconciliation: variance(D) <= 1.0% daily overall; rolling 7-day variance <= 0.5%.

Paging policy:
- Page if partition missing 2h after deadline OR final completeness misses OR reconciliation > 1.5%.
- Slack-only if provisional completeness misses or variance between 1.0–1.5%.

Allison Grant: Works for me. Please make sure the monitor messages include “owner + next step” so whoever gets paged doesn’t have to hunt. Ex: “Primary: @telemetry-oncall; runbook: <link>; dashboard: <link>”.

Caleb Johnson: I’ll wire monitors with templated links + add `@pagerduty-telemetry-analytics` for paging. Also adding a “mute during planned backfill” note.

Aisha Bello: I’ll draft the SLO doc in Confluence with the above + escalation path and share for sign-off. Once we have the runbook link in place, we can flip paging on. :thumbsup:

Priya Natarajan: Great. Let’s target end of week for: SLO doc + monitors in Slack (no paging). Paging turn-on after 1 week of observing noise levels.

Allison Grant: +1. Thanks all. Please thread the final SLO numbers in the ENG-2917 ticket so we don’t lose them.
